title: Count the neighbours
description:
A tile map is stored as one flat string, row after row, `width` tiles per row.

Write `countAround(tiles, width, x, y, wanted)`. It returns how many of the eight tiles around `(x, y)` equal `wanted`. Tiles outside the map do not count, and the tile at `(x, y)` itself does not count.

```
tiles = "#.#"
        "..."
        "#.#"        (stored as "#.#...#.#", width 3)

countAround(tiles, 3, 1, 1, '#')  = 4
countAround(tiles, 3, 0, 0, '.')  = 3
```

The number of rows is `tiles.size() / width`.
hints: Two loops, `dx` and `dy`, each from -1 to 1, visit the nine tiles of the 3 by 3 block. Skip the one where both are 0.

Before reading a neighbour, check it is inside the map: `nx` from 0 to `width - 1`, `ny` from 0 to `height - 1`. Without the check on `nx`, a tile on the right edge would "see" the start of the next row.
The index of `(nx, ny)` in the flat string is `ny * width + nx`.
lessonTitle: Arrays and Multi-Dimensional Data in Memory
